stem.text: Selected values of a function f are given in the table. The function f is not defined at \( x = 1 \). What does the table suggest about \( \lim_{x \to 1} f(x) \)?

answer_key.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs keep alternating as x approaches 1.

worked_solution.text: On each side the outputs switch between 0 and -3 however close x comes to 1.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: The outputs do not settle toward any single value, so the table suggests the limit does not exist.
worked_solution.rule_named: limit requires the outputs to settle

options.label: The table suggests that the limit is 0, because the outputs keep returning to 0.
options.derivation: one of the two values the outputs alternate between reported as the limit

options.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs keep alternating as x approaches 1.
The table suggests that the limit is -3, because the outputs keep returning to -3.
options.derivation: the other of the two values the outputs alternate between reported as the limit

options.derivation: nonexistence concluded from f being undefined at the target rather than from the outputs
